title: Validator‑Guided Repair on a Shared Initial LLM Candidate: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation for Network Configuration Safety
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) to measure the effect of a deterministic network‑configuration validator with an allowed single automated repair on the exact same sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using the declared generator gpt‑5‑mini (hosted adapter label openai_responses) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 over N = 200 paired intents (completed_episode_count = 400; model_calls_used = 200), every shared initial candidate passed validator checks so no repairs were attempted or applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Observed outcomes: baseline_success = 200/200, guarded_success = 200/200; paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. We present artifact‑grounded methodology, execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, an explicit repair summary, and a focused discussion clarifying the causal limits of the executed estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics and preregistered follow‑on designs required to measure repair efficacy under independent sampling, increased difficulty, or adversarial inputs.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration sequences in network operations (NetOps). Mistakes at the configuration level (syntax errors, incorrect sequencing, fabricated fields) can produce service disruption or policy violations when applied to devices. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→repair (GVR): produce one or more candidate configurations; use a deterministic validator to detect violations against intent, topology, and workflow constraints; and apply automated repairs only when the validator detects faults. Prior work documents verifier‑guided improvements in adjacent domains (infrastructure‑as‑code, program repair) and recommends grounding strategies to reduce hallucination in operational text tasks [see Related Work]. However, transfer from these domains to execution‑level NetOps safety (whether generated command sequences would be unsafe when enacted) is not established in the verified literature. Accordingly, we designed a narrowly scoped, fully preregistered paired experiment that isolates the causal effect of deterministic validation and any permitted repair on the exact same sampled generator output per intent. The research question we executed is precise: under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled generation deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded episodes), does permitting a deterministic validator plus up to one automated repair change the proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations relative to leaving the identical candidate unguarded?
sections.related_work: Surveys and empirical reports document widespread LLM hallucination and motivate grounding and verification for operational applications [1]. Retrieval‑augmented and evidence‑grounded pipelines reduce hallucination rates in QA/documentation tasks but typically evaluate textual correctness rather than device‑level executability in packet‑level simulation or emulation [2]. Generate→verify→repair architectures have shown improvements in IaC or program repair contexts and directly motivated our methodological approach [3]. NetOps‑focused evaluations examine intent translation and model capability but generally do not standardize execution‑level safety measures that map generated commands to executable device states; AIOps surveys highlight the need for execution‑aware benchmarks and stronger validator fidelity to bridge model outputs to operational safety [4,5]. From these verified sources we derived two empirical gaps that informed study selection: (1) verifier‑guided improvements in IaC do not directly demonstrate execution‑level safety for network device configurations, and (2) many prior proposals conflate generation sampling variability with downstream validator/repair effects, motivating a preregistered estimand that isolates the latter.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration, estimand, and design. The experiment was preregistered (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) before any model calls. The primary estimand is the paired difference in the proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations between guarded and baseline conditions under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Design: N = 200 paired intents (planned_episode_count = 400), one shared sampled generation per pair, and at most one automated repair permitted in the guarded arm (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). The primary statistical test was the exact two‑sided McNemar test; a paired bootstrap (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) was used to compute a percentile 95% confidence interval for the paired difference. The preregistration specified complete_pair_primary missingness treatment (exclude incomplete pairs) and a prespecified sensitivity analysis that would treat missing/failed episodes as unsafe.

Task bank, contamination checks, and selection. A deterministic task generator produced a fixed manifest of 200 synthetic "intent_configuration_repair_v1" tasks. Each manifest entry records initial_state, required_sequence, difficulty annotations (examples: "safe_access_service_transfer", "rolling_access_vlan_migration"), and a generation_seed for deterministic replay. Preexecution contamination checks (SHA‑256 exact‑match and n‑gram similarity rules) were run; no exact‑match exclusions were flagged and the confirmatory sample executed intact. The task manifest and contamination summary are archived in the execution bundle.

Generation semantics and model configuration. Execution used the declared generator labeled gpt‑5‑mini via the hosted adapter openai_responses. The execution manifest reports model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; we explicitly state that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Provider audit traces record hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Deterministic validator and repair policy. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring_rule = "full_intent_constraint_validation." The validator parses candidate command sequences, compares them against the task's required_sequence and workflow_policies, and emits a structured trace containing validation_before and validation_after subtables, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, violation_codes, and a repair_applied flag if a repair occurs. The guarded arm was permitted one automated repair invocation; under shared_initial_candidate semantics only the guarded arm could alter the identical candidate via that permitted repair. The validator's boolean valid flag was mapped to a binary "executable/valid" outcome for analysis.

Execution accounting, missingness, and analysis plan. The preregistration fixed maximum_model_calls = 400 but allowed the adapter to enforce resource limits; primary analyses used complete_pair_primary policy. The planned primary test (exact McNemar two‑sided) and paired bootstrap procedure were executed exactly as preregistered. Exploratory subgroup analyses (by difficulty patterns) were prespecified as exploratory and subject to Benjamini–Hochberg correction if performed.
sections.results:
Execution and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest reports planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 200. Analysis missingness_summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and records provider_call_audit values: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200}, and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false.

Primary outcomes and contingency. Condition summaries: baseline_successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency table: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. The analysis artifacts recording these numbers are analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv archived in the evidence bundle.

Repair activity and representative validator diagnostics. Across the confirmatory sample repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0: the validator flagged no violations on any shared initial candidate, so the guarded pipeline never invoked a repair. Representative per‑episode scoring JSON artifacts (examples: execution/scoring/task-000004-baseline.json and task-000004-guarded.json) show identical shared_initial_candidate text and identical validation_after.normalized_configuration values. Representative candidate excerpt (task-000004 shared initial candidate):

interface edge2 admin down
interface edge2 vlan 40
interface edge2 admin up
interface edge1 admin down

For that example parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, and validator.valid = true. Similar diagnostics for tasks 000005 and 000006 show parsed_command_count equaling required_command_count and validator.valid = true. The per‑episode validator traces, normalized configurations, and repair_applied flags are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ for independent inspection.

Provider audit and contamination summary. Preexecution contamination checks flagged no exact matches; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty. Provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and cache_miss_count = 200. No infrastructure failures or retries occurred; all deterministic consistency checks passed. The absence of validator detections fully explains the degenerate contingency: with no validator detections the permitted guarded repair path had no opportunity to change outcomes.

Reviewer‑requested compact repair summary (artifact‑grounded). Total_pairs = 200; repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0. These values derive directly from the per‑episode validator traces archived under execution/scoring/ and from analysis/condition_summary.csv.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and causal scope. Because the experiment executed shared_initial_candidate semantics, the causal estimand isolates the effect of deterministic validation and any permitted repair acting on the identical sampled generator output. Under these semantics any paired difference could only arise from deterministic validation and a permitted repair of that same candidate. The executed evidence shows no validator detections across the sampled candidates; therefore the guarded path was never exercised and the experiment cannot inform whether permitting repairs would reduce first‑pass generator error rates under independent sampling. Put plainly: this run answers whether validation/repair change outcomes for an identical candidate — it does not evaluate whether guarded pipelines change the distribution of generator outputs or first‑pass validity.

Threats to validity — artifact‑grounded elaboration. Internal validity: the paired design with shared_initial_candidate eliminates sampling variability between arms and preserves internal attribution for repair effects on the identical candidate; however, that attribution is vacuous here because no repairs were triggered. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performs syntactic and workflow policy checks and outputs a boolean valid flag; it is an abstracted deterministic verifier and does not execute vendor CLI on devices nor perform packet‑level emulation, so dynamic runtime interactions and time‑dependent protocol behaviors are outside its scope. External validity: the run used a single declared generator (gpt‑5‑mini via openai_responses), one synthetic deterministic task bank, and one validator implementation; therefore generalization beyond these artifacts is unsupported by the archived evidence. Conclusion validity: because all pairs were concordant (n11 = 200), no inferential evidence exists to estimate repair benefit magnitude under different sampling regimes where validator failures are present.

Operational implications and precise follow‑on estimands supported by artifacts. The null result does not imply GVR is unnecessary. Rather, it shows that under the executed task bank and single sampled candidate per pair the validator found no violations. To measure repair efficacy operationally we preregistered several concrete follow‑on estimand changes that the archived artifacts support: (A) remove shared_initial_candidate semantics so baseline and guarded arms receive independent first‑pass samples (this makes first‑pass generator variability observable and allows repairs to act on a broader set of faults but requires a revised paired/unpaired analysis plan); (B) select or synthesize tasks annotated as "extreme" difficulty or inject adversarial perturbations into generator prompts to raise expected validator failure rates and thereby exercise repair logic; (C) set explicit non‑null temperature values in model_configuration and preregister temperature sweeps to explore the tradeoff between generation diversity and validator failure rates; (D) increase validator fidelity by integrating vendor CLI semantics and packet‑level emulation so repair evaluation considers dynamic runtime behavior; (E) expand generator scope across model families to test generality. Each of these follow‑on designs can reuse the deterministic task bank, provider audit procedures, and validator interfaces archived in the execution bundle.

Reproducibility specifics (artifact pointers and deterministic checks). The execution evidence bundle contains: execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/responses/*.txt (shared, baseline, guarded), execution/scoring/*.json (per‑episode validator traces), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, and model_configuration.json. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts record all episode accounting numbers and provider_call_audit values (hosted_model_call_event_count = 200; cache_miss_count = 200; stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200}). The archived model_configuration.json includes declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null; as preregistered and documented in Methods, null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and cannot be interpreted as temperature = 0. The immutable master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). These artifacts permit exact replay of the executed estimand and verification that repairs were never invoked.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment that measured whether a deterministic validator plus an allowed single automated repair can change the validator‑valid outcome of the exact same sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using gpt‑5‑mini via openai_responses on 200 paired intents, every shared initial candidate passed validation so no repairs were attempted or applied; baseline and guarded outcomes were identical (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]). This artifact‑grounded null result demonstrates an estimand boundary: under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the executed task bank the guarded pipeline could not change outcomes because the validator flagged zero violations. It does not imply that GVR pipelines are unnecessary in practice. Preregistered follow‑on experiments that (1) remove shared_initial_candidate semantics, (2) increase task difficulty or inject adversarial inputs, (3) set explicit sampling parameters (temperature), and (4) raise validator fidelity are necessary to empirically evaluate repair efficacy under realistic sampling variability and adversarial conditions. Concise reiteration: the executed estimand measured downstream validator/repair effects on identical sampled candidates only; independent per‑condition sampling would constitute a different preregistered estimand and requires a different execution plan. Reviewer‑requested one‑line repair summary: total_pairs = 200; repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0.

After the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature review, experiment selection, preregistration (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01), code generation, execution, deterministic validation, automated analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting without manual human editing of technical content. Declared model used in execution: gpt‑5‑mini via hosted adapter 'openai_responses' (execution used model_calls_used = 200; archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Generation semantics executed: shared_initial_candidate — exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded conditions. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored candidates using 'full_intent_constraint_validation' and one automated repair iteration was permitted in guarded episodes; in this run the validator flagged no violations and no repairs were applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Execution accounting: completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired intents) completed without preregistration deviations. Immutable master prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Pre‑lock infrastructure development and rehearsal occurred but pre‑lock artifacts were not used as empirical evidence in this final run. After the autonomy lock no human manually rewrote technical results, manuscript text, figures, or references.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design produced exactly one sampled initial generation per intent and reused it across baseline and guarded conditions; this measures validator/repair effects only and cannot detect differences caused by independent per‑condition sampling or prompt engineering.

Temperature unset (temperature = null) in the archived model configuration: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still have occurred during the single sampled generation.
Single model and single hosted provider: results reflect gpt‑5‑mini under the archived adapter; generalization to other models or model families is unsupported by these artifacts.

Synthetic task bank and validator abstraction: tasks were synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' items and the deterministic validator is an abstraction; realistic vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, emergent runtime interactions, and hardware effects were not executed on live devices.

No observed validator failures: all initial candidates were validator‑valid, so the experiment could not assess the repair step's effectiveness; the null effect therefore reflects the task bank and sampling semantics rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.
